newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former HK judge gets thumbs up in leadership race.
newsitem.headline: Former HK judge gets thumbs up in leadership race.

text.p: Hong Kong's ex-chief justice Ti Liang Yang, running for leadership in the territory after the British depart next year, was given the thumbs up on Thursday in a popularity poll, Pearl television station reported.
The poll, conducted by the University of Hong Kong and which surveyed 576 people, gave Yang 66 percent of votes, ahead of shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, who scored 63 percent.
The poll asked which of eight candidates running for Hong Kong's first post-handover leader they would wish to be retained in the selection process.
However, Hong Kong people will not be casting votes for their leader. The chief executive will be chosen by a China-appointed, 400-member Selection Committee.
The committee, convening for the first time on Friday, would make a shortlist of the eight candidates.
To enter the final race for the job, a candidate must be nominated by at least 50 members of the committee. The committee meets again on December 11 to pick the winner.
Businessman Peter Woo garnered third highest number of votes with 50.3 percent and former judge Simon Li had 44.8 percent.
The other four lesser known candidates had less than three percent each, the television station reported.
The chief executive will succeed governor Chris Patten at midnight on June 30 when Britain hands the territory back to China.
